text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The Central Bank has written to the Finance Ministry expressing concern over growth in the Norwegian economy. It said it not exclude a potential change in monetary policy.
- Kristian Brenden won a World Cup ski jumping event in Lillehammer on Sunday making the first Norwegian World Cup ski jumping victory since February, 1995.
- Alpine skiier Tom Stiansen won Sunday's World Cup slalom in Beckenridge in the United States. It was Stiansen's first World Cup victory.

- Kvaerner ASA is one of the contenders to win a contract to build a production ship for Essos's Jotun oilfield. The contract will possibly be shared between Kvaerner's Masa-Yards in Finland and Kvaerner Rosenborg in Norway.

- Norway's largest banks are clarifying a system for trading shares on the Internet. Christiania og Kreditkassen has the most elaborate plans so far, but Helge Rangnes, head of Christiania's information department, cannot say when the bank will be ready to trade shares on the Internet.
